mainEntity.name: How do I turn an AI capability into an offer people will actually understand?

acceptedAnswer.text:
AI should support the offer’s delivery or decision-making process, not serve as the offer by itself. A buyer usually pays for a useful result—such as a researched brief, finished lesson plan, qualified follow-up sequence, or organized workflow—not for access to vague AI capabilities.

Context: Strong positioning connects a defined audience and problem to a specific deliverable. Run My AI Business examples include opportunity research, course planning, lead magnets, sales funnels, and operational checks.

Key factors:
- The customer’s current workaround
- The deliverable they can evaluate
- Where human expertise remains necessary
- Whether the workflow reduces time, confusion, or repeated effort

Practical guidance: Write the offer as “I help [audience] achieve [result] through [defined process].” Then list inputs, review points, turnaround expectations, and exclusions.

Use AI education to clarify the promise and workflow while keeping the buyer’s outcome at the center.
acceptedAnswer.description: Package AI around a customer result, not around the technology. Define the audience, problem, deliverable, inputs, review process, and boundaries. Buyers are more likely to understand a researched brief, course outline, or follow-up system than a general promise to “use AI for growth.”
